thread:
anna (Support): Customer reports streaming responses drop after ~18-25s when requests travel through a gRPC -> HTTP/1.1 gateway (third-party proxy chain). They see a partial payload, client reconnects, then either duplicate tokens or truncated continuation. They attached a client log and say they were billed for the partial stream. Ticket SUP-8432.

olivia (Customer Success): Customer is on Dedicated; says this started after a network appliance update last week. They can repro reliably from their side. Wants a quick workaround and a billing credit if it's on our side. :sweat:

anna (Support): repro steps requested - client details, headers, and a raw curl reproduction.

diego (Eng-Gateway): Can you paste the exact request/headers they used? Suspect intermediary is buffering flushes and then an upstream RST/CANCEL on reconnect. If we can repro with curl we can narrow whether it's gateway translation (gRPC->HTTP1) vs an intermediate cache.

anna (Support): Customer sent this minimal repro (sanitized):
```bash
# HTTP/2 client to our gateway (upstream is gRPC backend behind envoy)
curl -v --http2 \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <JWT>" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" \\n  "https://api.customer.example/v1/stream?model=llm-test"
```
They also tried forcing HTTP/1.1 with `--http1.1` and said behavior changes (less truncation but higher latency).

matt (SRE): Attach gateway logs around the time of request. Look for RST_STREAM or ECONNRESET between client and upstream. Also check proxy buffering configs - nginx `proxy_buffering` or Envoy `buffered_stream`.

diego (Eng-Gateway): I pulled the gateway trace. Upstream (our runtime) is sending multiple flushes as tokens are generated (we call them FRAME flushes). Envoy in front of the gRPC backend is aggregating small DATA frames because of its buffering policy and then, on client reconnect, sends `RST_STREAM` to terminate the old stream. The client only receives the last aggregated chunk (partial tokens). The RST -> reconnect sequence makes the client resend and we sometimes produce duplicate tokens which the customer sees as billing for both attempts.

anna (Support): Customer included connect logs from their client showing `HTTP/2 RST_STREAM` with code CANCEL and a small `Content-Length` change on the reconnect.

olivia (Customer Success): Billing asked for a clear explanation before issuing credits. We need a concrete repro and a mitigation we can ship to the customer ASAP.

billing-bot: Policy note: usage is billable for tokens our runtime emitted and the gateway forwarded. If duplicate emissions occur due to retries, support can issue ad-hoc credits. Please provide token ids/time ranges.

matt (SRE): Immediate mitigation suggestions for the customer: ask them to force HTTP/1.1 for the streaming route from their client: `curl --http1.1 --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" ...` which reduces the intermediary's http2 frame handling and tends to avoid envoy aggregation. Also recommend they set `Connection: keep-alive` and ensure no client-side timeout < 60s.

diego (Eng-Gateway): For our side, two approaches:
1) Short-term: set streaming routes in the gateway to disable buffering. Nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` Envoy: configure the filter to disable response buffering for streaming endpoints (we'll add a route option to not buffer). This preserves flush semantics so the client sees partial tokens as they arrive.
2) Longer-term: update the gRPC->HTTP1 translation layer to emit explicit chunk boundaries and a small keepalive ping frame so intermediaries don't coalesce.

anna (Support): Customer tried `--http1.1` and said it "improves but doesn't eliminate" the partial outputs; they still saw occasional reconnects when their network path included a third-party load balancer.

diego (Eng-Gateway): That matches a buffered intermediate. Can you ask the customer to run this reproducible curl (we provided):
```bash
# force http1.1 and disable client buffering to demonstrate behavior
curl -v --http1.1 --no-buffer \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <JWT>" \\n  "https://api.customer.example/v1/stream?model=llm-test"
```
Watch for partial chunks and `RST_STREAM` in `-v` output. If they capture a tcpdump of the last 30s we can correlate frames.

matt (SRE): Action items for infra: audit all edge proxies for response buffering settings (nginx/HAProxy/Envoy) and identify any that were changed in the past 7 days. If we find a change, roll back or pin a per-route override to disable buffering for streaming APIs.

olivia (Customer Success): I'll ask the customer for tcpdump and will offer a one-time billing credit if we confirm our proxy caused duplicate emissions. Also offering a short-lived configuration flag to turn off buffering on their Dedicated gateway while eng works on a fix.

diego (Eng-Gateway): We can push a canary that sets `route: { disable_response_buffering: true }` for the customer's gateway. That should preserve flush semantics without a full platform deploy. We'll test with internal repro first.

anna (Support): Recording repro steps + what customer saw into SUP-8432. Leaving the customer the quick curl and the temporary workaround (force http1.1 or request disable_response_buffering).

billing-bot: Please attach the customer's token usage and timestamps so finance can compute any credits.

matt (SRE): Preliminary root-cause hypothesis: an intermediary started aggregating HTTP/2 DATA frames which combined small flushes into larger TCP segments. When the stream was cancelled, only the last aggregated payload reached the client; earlier frames were lost from the client's perspective. This caused the app to reconnect and re-request, producing duplicate token emissions.

diego (Eng-Gateway): Next: I'll create a small canary and test against the customer's repro. If successful, we schedule a controlled rollout and update docs about streaming route config (note the nginx/envoy knobs).

olivia (Customer Success): Thanks team — telling customer we can canary disable buffering and will follow up within 4 hours. Offering a provisional credit pending confirmation.

anna (Support): Closing loop: please post results in this thread after canary test. If we confirm, mark SUP-8432 as escalated to P1 for the Dedicated customer.

-- end of thread --
